name: Martyrdom of Boniface, Apostle of Germany
summary: Boniface (Wynfrith), the English monk who organized the German church and reformed the Frankish church under Carolingian patronage, is martyred in Frisia while on a missionary journey. His work founding monasteries at Fulda and Reichenau and organizing the German dioceses creates the ecclesiastical framework for Charlemagne's German empire.

_quarry.structural_significance: Boniface's church organization gives Charlemagne the episcopal network through which to govern; Fulda becomes the leading intellectual center in Carolingian Germany; the Frankish-papal alliance Boniface brokered enables Pepin's seizure of the throne.
